# [Baseline] - AND - U - Compliance Device Health

Marks an Android device with a personal work profile as non-compliant when it is rooted, USB debugging is enabled, apps from outside the Play Store are allowed, Play Integrity cannot be confirmed with hardware backing, or the latest security patch is older than the minimum.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Android |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Compliance |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | OpenIntuneBaseline convention for compliance, content compared with IntuneAdmin (Personally-owned work profile - Device Health) and UniFy-Endpoint Android BYOD. |
| File | [`Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Device_Health.json`](Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Device_Health.json) |

> Written as `androidWorkProfileCompliancePolicy` — the personal work profile. `hardwareBacked` excludes older devices without supported hardware attestation — that is intended, but check it against the fleet before you assign. Since September 2026 this policy also requires a security patch of 2026-03-01 or later (six months back, the same as the warning in App Protection); devices from manufacturers that patch quarterly stay well within it. The OS minimum (12.0) and the patch date go stale: run `node scripts/check-osversion.js` to see how far behind they are. Both are currency targets (see `ondergrens`) and may move along, but not without checking how many devices fall below them. Defender for Endpoint is deliberately in a separate policy (Compliance Defender for Endpoint), because it requires a licence and connector.
